Dear colleagues,

Further to the discussion at Tuesday's steering committee, I am writing to
summarise the position regarding the proposed migration of the reporting
platform, and to set out the recommended sequence of activities for the coming
quarter.

The review team has now completed its assessment of the three candidate
approaches. Each was evaluated against the criteria agreed in March, namely
total cost of ownership, operational risk, and the degree of disruption
anticipated during transition. The assessment was conducted by the platform
group with input from finance and from the regional operations leads.

It should be noted that the first approach, a phased migration undertaken over
eighteen months, was assessed as carrying the lowest operational risk.
Nevertheless, the cost implications are considerable, and the extended timeline
would require the existing platform to be maintained in parallel for a
substantial period. Furthermore, the resourcing model assumed in that estimate
has not been validated with the delivery function.

The second approach, a single transition undertaken during the December
maintenance window, would be materially less expensive. However, the
concentration of risk within a single weekend is difficult to justify given the
reporting obligations that fall due in January. Were the transition to fail, the
consequences for regulatory reporting would be significant.

Accordingly, the review team recommends the third approach. Under this option,
the reporting platform would be migrated in two stages, with the historical
archive transferred first and the live reporting functions transferred
subsequently, once the archive has been verified. This sequencing permits
verification to be undertaken without affecting current operations, and it
allows the project to be halted at the stage boundary should the verification
results prove unsatisfactory.

A detailed implementation plan will be circulated in advance of the next
committee meeting. In the interim, I would be grateful if departmental leads
could confirm the availability of their nominated representatives for the
workshop scheduled for the fourteenth.

I should like to record my appreciation for the work undertaken by the review
team, which was completed within a demanding timeframe and to a high standard.

Should you require any clarification regarding the foregoing, please do not
hesitate to contact me directly.

Kind regards,

The Programme Office
